# bide command reference

<!-- Generated by TestCLIReference in cmd/bide from the flag sets the commands parse. Do not edit:
     run go test . -run TestCLIReference -update in cmd/bide. CI fails when this page is stale. -->

One program, `bide`, for everyone who does not import the library. Install it with
`brew install bide-ai/tap/bide` or `go install github.com/bide-ai/bide/cmd/bide@latest`.

Every command parses its own flags with the standard library `flag` package: flags take
one dash (`-db`, `-evidence`), and `bide help <command>` or
`bide <command> -h` prints what is below. Exit status is 0 for success, 1 for a failure and
2 for a usage error, for every command but `bide audit`, which keeps its own statuses:
only 0 means verified.

On a terminal the text output is colored (a green ✓ and a red ✗ beside the words, never instead
of them); written to a file or a pipe it is plain. `-color=auto|always|never` sets it, and
`NO_COLOR` (any value) or `TERM=dumb` turns `auto` off.

Built with `-tags bide_audit_only`, the program holds only `audit`, `version`
and `help`, and its import graph is the standard library and the core module (see the
[security model](../guides/security-model.md)).

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`bide init`](#bide-init) | scaffold a project: a gated plan flow on SQLite, with evidence for bide audit |
| [`bide demo`](#bide-demo) | kill an agent mid-payment and watch it not charge twice (no API key) |
| [`bide view`](#bide-view) | a read-only local page for one run of a journal, or a flow config's graph |
| [`bide check`](#bide-check) | check plan flow configs, for CI: one file:node: message line per problem |
| [`bide audit`](#bide-audit) | produce and verify audit proofs offline |
| [`bide version`](#bide-version) | print the version and the artifact formats bide audit reads (-json for JSON) |

## bide init

Scaffold a project: a gated plan flow on SQLite, with evidence for bide audit.

```text
usage: bide init [-module <path>] [-dev <bide checkout>] <dir>

Writes a new project into dir, which must not exist or must be empty: main.go, main_test.go,
flow.yaml, README.md, .gitignore and go.mod. Then: cd <dir> && go mod tidy && go run .

  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never
  -dev string
    	a bide checkout to build against (replace directives), for a bide built from source
  -module string
    	the module path (default: the directory's name)

Exit status:
  0  success
  1  failure: an input cannot be read or the command failed; for check, an error was found
     (with -strict, any problem)
  2  usage error: a bad flag or argument; nothing was read
```

## bide demo

Kill an agent mid-payment and watch it not charge twice (no API key).

```text
Usage of bide demo:
  -addr string
    	loopback address to serve the viewer on (port 0 picks a free one) (default "127.0.0.1:0")
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never
  -fast
    	no pauses between steps (for CI)
  -keep
    	keep the demo's directory (the journal, evidence and keys) and print it
  -no-browser
    	print the viewer's address instead of opening a browser

Exit status:
  0  success
  1  failure: an input cannot be read or the command failed; for check, an error was found
     (with -strict, any problem)
  2  usage error: a bad flag or argument; nothing was read
```

## bide view

A read-only local page for one run of a journal, or a flow config's graph.

```text
bide view: a read-only local web page for one run of a bide journal

  bide view -db <file> [-run <id>] [flags]
  bide view -postgres <dsn> [-run <id>] [flags]
  bide view -journal <export.json> [-journal ...] [-run <id>] [flags]
  bide view -config <flow.yaml|flow.json> [-check [-strict]]
  bide view -config <flow.yaml|flow.json> -diff <old config|git revision> [-check [-fail-on-weaken]]

It shows an agent run's timeline (model turns, tool calls with their Safety, attempts, approvals,
halts, end state) or a plan flow's declared topology with the run's path (drawn from the topology
the run journaled, its digest checked, unless -topology overrides it), and whether the journal
verifies against a signed tree head or an evidence package; with -approver-keys, whether each
m-of-n approval gate's signatures verify (audit.VerifyApprovals), against the policy the gate
recorded or, with -need and -approvers, against the policy you expect. It never writes to the
store, and it serves on a loopback address only. Stop it with Ctrl-C.

With no -run the page opens on the run list: each run's kind, state (completed, halted: outcome
unknown, waiting for approval, in progress, aborted or cancelled), when it started (as its
run:start records it; none for a run an earlier version journaled) and its record count, newest
first, filtered by state, kind and run ID.

From -db or -postgres, the page of a run in progress follows it (live mode): it polls the store
about once a second for records after the last one it shows, and updates in place until the run
journals its end marker. An exported journal (-journal) is shown as it is.

With -config it shows a flow definition instead, without running anything: the declared graph,
its approval gates, and every problem plan.InspectConfig finds, marked on the node, edge or arm it
belongs to. The check is structural (types and registered blocks are checked when a program embeds
the viewer with its plan.Registry, see package plan/planview). Each node is colored by its crash
behavior (side effect, read-only, idempotent, or unknown without the Registry), and the config's
assert lines are decided on the graph, a violated one's counterexample path drawn in red. With
-check it serves nothing and prints one "file:node: message" line per problem ("file:from->to:
message" for an edge or arm), a violated assertion among them.

With -diff it compares the -config flow with an earlier version of it: the page draws the new flow
with added nodes and edges in green, removed ones as dashed red ghosts and changed nodes in amber,
and calls out an approval gate whose policy was weakened (removed, its need lowered, or an approver
added without raising the need). -diff takes a file, or, when no file has that name, a git
revision read with git show: <rev>:<path>, or a bare <rev> for the -config file's path at that
revision. With -check it serves nothing and prints one line per change and a summary line.

Exit status: 0 after a clean stop (or -h, or a -check that found no errors; warnings do not
count unless -strict; for -diff -check, a diff is not a failure), 1 if an input cannot be read,
the server fails, -check found errors (or, with -strict, any problem), or -diff -check
-fail-on-weaken found a weakened approval policy, 2 for a usage error.

Flags:
  -addr string
    	address to serve on: a loopback IP (127.0.0.1 or ::1) or localhost, with a port (default "127.0.0.1:8484")
  -approver-keys string
    	approver public keys, a JSON object of approver id to key text, e.g. {"ops":"ed25519:ab12..."}, to verify each m-of-n gate's signatures (audit.VerifyApprovals); needs -sth or -evidence
  -approvers string
    	the expected policy's approver ids, comma-separated, in policy order; needs -need
  -check
    	with -config: serve nothing, print each problem as file:node: message, and exit 1 if any is an error; with -diff, print each change instead
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never
  -config string
    	a flow config (.json, or .yaml/.yml) to show instead of runs: its declared graph and its problems; nothing runs
  -db string
    	SQLite journal file to read, opened read-only (sqlite.OpenReadOnly)
  -diff string
    	with -config: compare it with this earlier version, a file or else a git revision (<rev>:<path>, or <rev> for the -config path at rev); -check prints the changes instead of serving the page
  -digest string
    	flow.Digest() of the -topology flow, compared with the digest the run journaled (default: computed from -topology when it carries the digest's inputs)
  -evidence string
    	evidence package (audit.EvidencePackage JSON) to verify; needs -pubkey
  -fail-on-weaken
    	with -diff -check: exit 1 if an approval gate was removed or weakened
  -journal value
    	exported journal (audit.ExportJournal as JSON) to read; repeatable
  -need int
    	the expected policy's k: verify approvals against -need of -approvers instead of the recorded policy; needs -approvers and -approver-keys
  -postgres string
    	Postgres journal to read, a pgx DSN such as postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db, read in sessions the server holds read-only (postgres.OpenReadOnly)
  -pubkey string
    	log public key as <scheme>:<hex>, or bare ed25519 hex, or a file holding it
  -run string
    	run to open (default: the run list)
  -sth string
    	signed tree head (audit.SignedTreeHead JSON) to verify the journal against; needs -pubkey
  -strict
    	with -check: exit 1 on a warning too
  -topology string
    	declared flow topology, JSON of flow.Topology(), to draw a flow run against instead of the topology the run journaled (flow:topology); for a run journaled before that record existed, or to check a run against another flow

Exit status:
  0  success
  1  failure: an input cannot be read or the command failed; for check, an error was found
     (with -strict, any problem)
  2  usage error: a bad flag or argument; nothing was read
```

## bide check

Check plan flow configs, for CI: one file:node: message line per problem.

```text
usage: bide check [-strict] <flow.yaml|flow.json>...
       bide check <flow.yaml|flow.json> -diff <old config|git revision> [-check [-fail-on-weaken]]

Checks each plan flow config without running it, and prints one "file:node: message" line per
problem ("file:from->to: message" for an edge or arm). The check is structural: types and
registered blocks are checked when a program serves the page with its plan.Registry (package
plan/planview). It is the check bide view -config shows on the graph.

A config's assert lines are checked too, by reachability on the declared graph:

  every path to <node> passes approval >= K [of N]
  every path to <node> passes <node>
  every path to a terminal passes <node>
  no side effect after <node>
  <node> reachable
  <node> unreachable

A violated assertion is an error, printed with a shortest counterexample path ("counterexample:
a -> b -> c"); so is an assertion that is not in this grammar, names an undeclared node, or cannot
be decided. A file with assertions ends with a line counting their verdicts.

With -diff it compares the config with an earlier version of it instead, and serves a read-only
local page (like bide view) that draws the new flow with added nodes and edges in green, removed
ones as dashed red ghosts and changed nodes in amber, and calls out a weakened approval policy.
-diff takes a file; when no file has that name, a git revision read with git show: <rev>:<path>
(git's own form), or a bare <rev> for the config's own path at that revision (bide check
flows/refund.yaml -diff main). With -check it serves nothing, prints one line per change and a
summary line, and exits 0: a diff is not a failure, unless -fail-on-weaken finds an approval gate
removed or weakened. Flags may follow the file names.

On a terminal the output is colored (a red cross on each error and its counterexample path in red,
a green check on assertions that all hold); piped or redirected it is plain text. -color=never, or
NO_COLOR set to any value, turns color off; -color=always keeps it on.

  -addr string
    	with -diff: address to serve the page on, a loopback IP (127.0.0.1 or ::1) or localhost, with a port (default "127.0.0.1:8484")
  -check
    	with -diff: serve nothing and print each change, then a summary line
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never
  -diff string
    	compare the one config given with this earlier version: a file, or else a git revision (<rev>:<path>, or <rev> for the config's path at rev)
  -fail-on-weaken
    	with -diff -check: exit 1 if an approval gate was removed or weakened (its need lowered, or an approver added without raising the need)
  -strict
    	exit 1 on a warning too

Exit status:
  0  success
  1  failure: an input cannot be read or the command failed; for check, an error was found
     (with -strict, any problem)
  2  usage error: a bad flag or argument; nothing was read
```

## bide audit

Produce and verify audit proofs offline.

```text
bide audit: produce and verify audit proof bundles

  bide audit [-json] <verb> [flags]
  bide audit -version [-json]

  prove  -journal <file> -sth <file> (-tool <id> | -index <n>) [-out <file>]
         build a ProofBundle for one record against a signed tree head

  verify -bundle <file> -pubkey <hex|file>
         verify a ProofBundle offline (its head must be a journal head of the bundle's run)

  verify-governance -policy <file> [-digest <hex>] [-checker <astchecker>]
         recompute the policy digest and, with -checker, run the external verified
         oracle to certify the policy converges

  verify-governed-action -action <bundle> -policy-bundle <bundle> -pubkey <hex|file> [-checker <astchecker>]
         verify a governed action end to end: both bundles authentic and in the same
         signed tree, the action's policy digest links to the anchored policy leaf, the
         leaf's bytes hash to that digest, and (with -checker) the policy converges

  verify-convergence -cert-bundle <bundle> -policy-bundle <bundle> -pubkey <hex|file> [-checker <astchecker>]
         verify an anchored convergence certificate: both bundles authentic and in the same
         signed tree, the certificate certifies the anchored policy's digest, the leaf's bytes
         hash to that digest, and (with -checker) the external oracle's verdict AGREES with the
         certificate's convergence claim, so a certificate that overstates convergence is caught

  verify-quorum -name <quorum> -tally <bundle> -vote <bundle> [-vote <bundle>...] -pubkey <hex|file> -k <n> [-commit <bundle>]
         verify a governed k-of-n quorum: the tally and every vote bundle authentic, in the
         same signed tree and run, and recorded by the quorum named <quorum>; every vote the
         tally records disclosed exactly once; the recorded tally recomputes from the disclosed
         votes (a forged tally is caught); and votes_for >= k; with -commit, a governed commit
         is anchored in the same tree

  verify-run -cert <file> -pubkey <hex|file> [-approved <digest>...] [-approved-file <file>] [-checker <astchecker>]
         (at least one of -approved and -approved-file; together they form one allowlist)
         verify a proof-carrying run certificate: the used-policy set is bound by a signed
         used-policy head to this run and its journal tree, and is a subset of the approved
         allowlist (only-approved-policies), and every used policy has an anchored, digest-linked convergence certificate
         in the run's signed tree (policies-convergence-certified); with -checker, the external
         oracle's convergence verdict on each used policy must AGREE with its certificate

  verify-evidence -evidence <file> -pubkey <hex|file> [-approved <digest>...] [-approved-file <file>]
         verify a portable evidence package offline and print a plain-English report: the
         format, seal, key, and run binding, then one line per proven action (tool call, step,
         grant), plus the run certificate (checked against the given allowlist, required when
         the package carries one) and consistency proof if present

  verify-approvals -evidence <file> -pubkey <hex|file> -call <tool-use-id|node-key> -need <k>
                   -approvers <id,id,...> -approver-keys <file> [-approved <digest>...] [-approved-file <file>]
         verify an m-of-n human approval gate from an evidence package: the request, every
         decision the gate read, its recorded tally, and the call's result all verify under the
         log key in one signed tree; recounting the decisions with each approver's key (a JSON
         object of approver id to public key text, <scheme>:<hex>) against the exact call reproduces the
         recorded tally; the gate enforced the expected policy; and at least k approved. Every
         proof in the package must verify too, so a package carrying a run certificate needs the
         allowlist it is checked against (-approved / -approved-file, as for verify-evidence)

  prove-absent -journal <file> -sth <file> -key (tool:<id>|policy:<digest>) [-out <file>]
         prove a thing did NOT happen (no such tool call / no action under that policy)
         against a signed key-set head of the matching kind (see audit.SignAbsenceRoot)

  verify-absent -bundle <file> -pubkey <hex|file>
         verify an absence proof offline against a head of the key's own key set

Export a journal for `prove` and `prove-absent` with audit.ExportJournal(ctx, store, runID),
marshaled to JSON (format bide.audit.journal-export.v1: each record's stored bytes, verbatim). Every
JSON input is parsed strictly: a duplicate or case-variant key, an unknown field, or invalid UTF-8 is
an error; a bundle, certificate, package, journal export or signed tree head (at any depth) must
carry the "format" this version reads (one made by an older release is refused with a message
naming the format; -version lists them); and a public key is <scheme>:<hex>, where the scheme is
ed25519, ml-dsa-65 or ed25519+ml-dsa-65, or bare 64-digit ed25519 hex. The key's scheme must be the
scheme the artifact is signed under. Every verb takes -max-input-bytes <n>: an input file larger
than n bytes (default 268435456, 256 MiB) is an error, and none is read past the cap. Every signed
tree head an input carries must have a positive timestamp (Unix nanoseconds) no later than this
machine's clock plus -max-clock-skew <duration> (default 5m). Every verb takes -json: it prints one
JSON report on stdout (exit_code, result, verified, output, errors) instead of the text report. On a
terminal the text report is colored, with a VERIFIED or FAILED banner at its end; -color=never or
NO_COLOR turns that off, and a pipe, a file or -json is always plain.

Exit status. Only 0 means verified; treat every other status as a failure, and 4 as a failure,
never as a reason to retry (a tampered "format" field yields 4):
  0  verified (for prove and prove-absent: the artifact was written)
  1  read and understood, and not verified
  2  usage error: a bad flag or argument; nothing was read
  3  no verdict: the -checker gave none (it could not be started, exited with a status other
     than 0 or 1, was killed, or printed an unreadable compensation_free line), or an internal error
  4  an input is unreadable or unusable: a missing or unreadable file, one over -max-input-bytes,
     JSON that does not read strictly, an unknown or unsupported format, or an artifact of the
     wrong type for its flag
When several apply, 1 wins over 4, and 4 over 3: a verb reads every input and runs every check
that does not depend on an unusable one, so a tampered input is reported as 1 even beside an
unreadable one.

Exit status:
  0  verified (for prove and prove-absent: the artifact was written)
  1  read and understood, and not verified
  2  usage error: a bad flag or argument; nothing was read
  3  no verdict: the -checker gave none, or an internal error
  4  an input is unreadable or unusable
```

### bide audit prove

```text
Usage of bide audit prove:
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never; -json is never colored
  -index int
    	prove the record at this journal index (default -1)
  -journal string
    	path to the journal export JSON (audit.ExportJournal)
  -json
    	print one JSON report on stdout instead of the text report
  -max-clock-skew duration
    	how far past this machine's clock a signed head's timestamp may be (default 5m0s)
  -max-input-bytes int
    	the largest input file, in bytes, the verb reads; a larger one is an error (default 268435456)
  -out string
    	write the bundle here (default: stdout)
  -sth string
    	path to the signed tree head JSON
  -tool string
    	prove the tool call with this ToolUseID
```

```text
Usage of bide audit prove-absent:

  -journal string
```


### bide audit verify-approvals

```text
Usage of bide audit verify-approvals:
  -approved value
    	an approved policy digest for the package's run certificate; repeat once per allowed policy
  -approved-file string
    	path to a file of approved policy digests, one per line
  -approver-keys string
    	JSON object of approver id to public key text (<scheme>:<hex>, or bare ed25519 hex), e.g. {"ops":"ed25519:ab12..."}
  -approvers string
    	the policy's eligible approver ids, comma-separated, in policy order
  -call string
    	the gated call's tool-use id, or a gated plan flow node's key ("node:<name>", "node:iter:<n>:<name>")
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never; -json is never colored
  -evidence string
    	path to the EvidencePackage JSON carrying the approval evidence
  -json
    	print one JSON report on stdout instead of the text report
  -max-clock-skew duration
    	how far past this machine's clock a signed head's timestamp may be (default 5m0s)
  -max-input-bytes int
    	the largest input file, in bytes, the verb reads; a larger one is an error (default 268435456)
  -need int
    	approvals the policy requires (k)
  -pubkey string
    	the log's public key as <scheme>:<hex> (ed25519, ml-dsa-65, ed25519+ml-dsa-65) or bare ed25519 hex, or a path to a file containing it
```

```text
  -max-clock-skew duration
    	how far past this machine's clock a signed head's timestamp may be (default 5m0s)
  -max-input-bytes int
    	the largest input file, in bytes, the verb reads; a larger one is an error (default 268435456)
  -policy-bundle string
    	path to the policy-leaf ProofBundle JSON (from ProvePolicy)
  -pubkey string
    	public key as <scheme>:<hex> (ed25519, ml-dsa-65, ed25519+ml-dsa-65) or bare ed25519 hex, or a path to a file containing it
```

### bide audit verify-quorum

```text
Usage of bide audit verify-quorum:
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never; -json is never colored
  -commit string
    	path to the commit action ProofBundle JSON (optional)
  -json
    	print one JSON report on stdout instead of the text report
  -k int
    	the quorum threshold to assert: votes_for must be >= k
  -max-clock-skew duration
    	how far past this machine's clock a signed head's timestamp may be (default 5m0s)
  -max-input-bytes int
    	the largest input file, in bytes, the verb reads; a larger one is an error (default 268435456)
  -name string
    	the quorum's name, as passed to govern.Quorum
  -pubkey string
    	public key as <scheme>:<hex> (ed25519, ml-dsa-65, ed25519+ml-dsa-65) or bare ed25519 hex, or a path to a file containing it
  -tally string
    	path to the quorum tally ProofBundle JSON (the quorum/<name>/tally step)
  -vote value
    	path to one vote ProofBundle JSON (a quorum/<name>/vote/<voter> step); repeat once per voter
```

### bide audit verify-run

```text
Usage of bide audit verify-run:
  -approved value
    	an approved policy digest; repeat once per allowed policy
  -approved-file string
    	path to a file of approved policy digests, one per line
  -cert string
    	path to the RunCertificate JSON (from audit.CertifyRun)
  -checker string
    	path to the external verified oracle (astchecker); if set, its verdict must agree with each policy's certificate
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never; -json is never colored
  -json
    	print one JSON report on stdout instead of the text report
  -max-clock-skew duration
    	how far past this machine's clock a signed head's timestamp may be (default 5m0s)
  -max-input-bytes int
    	the largest input file, in bytes, the verb reads; a larger one is an error (default 268435456)
  -pubkey string
    	public key as <scheme>:<hex> (ed25519, ml-dsa-65, ed25519+ml-dsa-65) or bare ed25519 hex, or a path to a file containing it
```

## bide version

Print the version and the artifact formats bide audit reads (-json for JSON).

```text
usage: bide version [-json]
  -json
    	print the version and the artifact formats as JSON

Exit status:
  0  success
  1  failure: an input cannot be read or the command failed; for check, an error was found
     (with -strict, any problem)
  2  usage error: a bad flag or argument; nothing was read
```
